channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Armenia Overhauls Residency Permit Rules, Introducing New Investment Path
item.description: Armenia has implemented significant reforms to its "Law on Foreigners," altering permanent residency rules. The business route now requires three years of temporary residency first. A new direct path to a five-year permanent residency is available for significant economic investors, bypassing the standard business route.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Urges Global Attention to Mountain Ecosystem Protection
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is calling on the international community to focus more on protecting mountain ecosystems and increase funding for mountain nations. At the COP17 conference in Yerevan, Kyrgyzstan proposed establishing a special mountain program within the Global Environment Facility and a global center for mountain region sustainability in Bishkek.

item.title: Astana to Restrict Traffic and Conduct Military Aviation Flights November 5-7
item.description: Astana will temporarily restrict traffic on certain streets from November 5 to 7, 2026, due to preparations for international political events. Special state and law enforcement agencies, along with the Armed Forces of Kazakhstan, will ensure security. Military aviation training flights will also occur.

item.title: UK Police Arrest Over 100 Palestine Action Supporters During Protests
item.description: British police arrested at least 139 supporters of the Palestine Action movement during protests in London and Edinburgh. Authorities have arrested over 4,000 people since the group was outlawed in July 2025. Many arrested displayed signs supporting Palestine.

item.title: France Deploys 70,000 Police Officers for Halloween Amid Protests
item.description: France plans to deploy 70,000 police officers nationwide for Halloween celebrations, anticipating further anti-government protests. Recent unrest over living costs and budget deficits has led to riots and over $1 billion in damages. Concerns exist about protesters using masks.

item.title: Kazakhstan and OPEC+ Agree to Maintain December Oil Production Quotas
item.description: Key OPEC+ participants, including Kazakhstan, have preliminarily agreed to keep December oil production targets unchanged. This decision aligns with expectations of further policy adjustments being postponed until next year. The group is assessing member countries' production capacities to determine 2027 baseline levels.

item.title: Reservoir Explosion at Rogun Dam Construction Site in Tajikistan
item.description: An explosion occurred at a reservoir during the construction of the Rogun Dam in Tajikistan. Authorities claim no one was injured, while independent media report casualties. The State Supervision Service for Industrial and Mining Safety attributed the incident to a rupture in a technical water collection reservoir, which flooded workers in a tunnel. First aid was provided, and workers returned to their jobs.

item.title: Kazakhstan's processed agricultural exports increase, exceeding 54% of total
item.description: Kazakhstan's exports of value-added agricultural products are steadily growing. In the first eight months of 2026, processed agricultural exports reached $3.04 billion, a 35.1% increase year-on-year. Processed goods now account for 54.1% of total agricultural exports, indicating improved competitiveness.

item.title: Taliban Announce Over 400 Individuals Forcibly Returned to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban reported the forced return of 464 individuals, including 108 families, to Afghanistan. Returns occurred through multiple border crossings, including Torkham, Spin Boldak, Silk Bridge, and Islam Qala. Hamdullah Fitrat, deputy Taliban spokesperson, provided details on the numbers processed at each location.

item.title: UN-Habitat Aid Insufficient for Repairing Returnee Shelters in Herat
item.description: UN-Habitat is assisting vulnerable returnee families in Herat with shelter repairs, supported by the UN Special Trust Fund for Afghanistan. The program aims to provide security and dignity, but current aid is insufficient to meet the families' needs, according to the UN.

item.title: UN Special Representative Reaffirms Support for Afghanistan During Nangarhar Visit
item.description: Rabab Fatima, the UN Secretary-General’s Special Representative for Afghanistan, visited Nangarhar province and met with various stakeholders, including Taliban officials, women, elders, and businesspeople. She reaffirmed the UN's commitment to continued support for Afghanistan and discussed pressing needs and challenges.

item.title: Polish Prime Minister Refuses Compromise with President Amid Constitutional Dispute
item.description: Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk has rejected any compromise with President Andrzej Duda regarding the constitutional tribunal dispute. The President returned to Warsaw from Senegal and met with the tribunal's dismissed speaker, while Tusk criticized the move, vowing to uphold the rule of law.

item.title: New Nationwide Polio Vaccination Campaign to Begin Tomorrow in Afghanistan
item.description: A new polio vaccination campaign is set to launch across Afghanistan tomorrow. The initiative aims to combat the spread of polio within the country. Health officials are urging widespread participation to ensure the campaign's success.

item.title: Polish PM Tusk Accuses Russia of Supporting Opponents Amidst Political Crisis
item.description: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk accused Russia of fueling the current political crisis in Poland, stating that an "army of Russian bots" on the internet supports his opponents. Tusk criticized the Law and Justice party, President Andrzej Duda, and current President Karol Nawrocki for undermining the rule of law. He highlighted attempts to resolve issues with the Constitutional Tribunal being obstructed.

item.title: Kazakhstan Begins Phased Introduction of Electronic Entry Permit System
item.description: Kazakhstan commenced a phased rollout of the QazETA electronic entry permit system on November 1. Initially, it applies to citizens of visa-free countries and EAEU nations at Aktau airport and select land border crossings. The permit will become mandatory by July 1, 2027.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan Companies Sign Agreements Worth $95 Million
item.description: Companies from Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan have signed agreements and contracts totaling $95 million following a trade and economic mission in Bishkek. The agreements were reached during the Second Forum of Interregional Cooperation between the two countries. Discussions focused on export expansion and joint investment projects.

item.title: Criminal Case Launched Against Imarat Development Management in Tashkent
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated against the management of Imarat Development LLC in Tashkent. The company, based in Sergeli district, allegedly failed to inform buyers that homes were being built in the Tashkent region and did not return funds.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Corn Fields Exceed Astana's Area After 60% Growth
item.description: Corn cultivation in Kazakhstan has surged by 60% to 106,000 hectares, surpassing the area of Astana. This expansion is driven by the demand from new processing plants, including 'KazKrakhmal' in the Turkestan region, which processes 150,000 tons of corn annually. The Ministry of Agriculture reported this growth.

item.title: Kazakhstan Activist Launches Petition to Ban Religious Education for Minors
item.description: A Kazakhstani activist, Asel Tauhan, has launched a petition proposing a ban on religious education for children under 18. She argues that some religious materials may pose hidden threats to minors' safety and rights, including justifying early marriages and infringing on women's rights. The petition, titled 'Religion Can Wait Until 18,' aims to address concerns about the content of religious instruction.

item.title: FBI Accuses North Korea of Stealing Over $6 Billion from Binance
item.description: The FBI has accused North Korea of being behind a cyberattack on the Binance crypto exchange, resulting in the theft of over $6 billion. The exchange has pledged to cover financial losses and announced a phased resumption of withdrawals. The FBI linked the attack to North Korean cyber activity known as TraderTraitor.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces New Entry and Stay Regulations for Foreign Citizens
item.description: New regulations for the entry and stay of foreigners in Kazakhstan will be implemented starting November 1st at one airport and four vehicle checkpoints. Citizens from 85 countries will need an electronic permit via the QazETA system. The phased rollout begins November 1, 2026, at Aktau Airport and specific checkpoints, with international airports in Astana and Almaty to follow in 2027.

item.title: Two Men Arrested in Kostanay for Extorting 17 Million Tenge
item.description: Two men were apprehended in Kostanay while extorting 17 million tenge from a victim. According to investigators, they threatened the victim with violence to demand the money. Previously convicted individuals were caught receiving 4.4 million tenge.

item.title: Man Arrested for 15 Days in Almaty for Inciting Trucker Protest
item.description: A man in Almaty has been sentenced to 15 days in jail for calling on truck drivers to protest restrictions on truck axle loads. He urged drivers to stop working on November 1, arguing that heavy trucks are essential for the city's construction infrastructure.

item.title: Turkish Daesh Suspect Uğur Bahadır Arrested in Pakistan, Trained in Balochistan
item.description: Turkish national Uğur Bahadır, a suspected Daesh member, reportedly arrived in Islamabad and received training at a Daesh camp in Balochistan, Pakistan. Sources claim he was arrested in Pakistan in March 2025, contradicting Turkish media reports of a recent capture in the Afghanistan-Pakistan region.

item.title: 15 Years Since Taraz Terror Attack: How One Man Claimed Multiple Lives in Two Hours
item.description: Fifteen years ago, on November 12, 2011, a devastating terror attack struck Taraz, Kazakhstan. Armed assailant Maksat Kariev carried out multiple attacks, including a gun store robbery and shootings targeting police officers, resulting in seven deaths and injuries. Police Captain Gaziz Baitasov died protecting civilians.

item.title: Trump Reiterates Iran Seeks Deal, Claims Talks Progressing Well
item.description: President Trump stated Iran desires a deal and that negotiations are progressing well, though he expressed skepticism about their reliability. He reiterated claims about damaging Iran's military capabilities and threatened strikes on a nuclear facility.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Agricultural Product Exports Increased by 35 Percent
item.description: Kazakhstan is prioritizing the development of its deep processing sector for grain and increasing finished product exports. This year, exports of processed agricultural products grew by 35 percent. Six major investment projects totaling $4 billion are planned.

item.title: Nigeria Investigating Two Suspected Ebola Cases in Northeast Region
item.description: Nigeria's Centre for Disease Control is investigating two suspected Ebola cases in the country's northeast. The individuals are quarantined, and contact tracing is underway. Confirmation awaits laboratory test results, following the country's first Ebola case in over a decade last week.

item.title: Ukraine Forces Strike Russian Rocket Fuel Plant in Rostov Region
item.description: Ukraine's armed forces claim to have struck a plant in Russia's Rostov region producing solid fuel for missiles. The General Staff reported that attack drones and Neptune missiles were used, causing a fire and damaging production workshops. This action aims to reduce Russia's ability to shell Ukrainian settlements.

item.title: Protests in Germany escalate to riots, with Molotov cocktails and vandalism
item.description: Youth protests organized by the 'Gen-Z regelt' movement in major German cities have turned violent. In Frankfurt, protesters smashed shop windows and clashed with police. Berlin reported 56 arrests, while Cologne banned a march. Over 100,000 participated nationwide.

item.title: FBI blames North Korean group TraderTraitor for Binance hack and $6 billion theft
item.description: The FBI has accused the North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor of stealing over $6 billion from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance. The group is reportedly converting stolen assets into Ethereum and laundering them through DeFi services. The FBI has published wallet addresses and urged sector participants to block transactions.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Upgrade Airports: New Runways and Terminals Planned by 2029
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to upgrade runways in seven airports and build new ones in Astana, Shymkent, and Aktobe by 2029. Reconstruction of existing runways is scheduled for Almaty, Zhezqazgan, Taraz, and Uralsk. Passenger terminals will also be modernized in Aktobe and six other cities, affecting a total of 12 airports.

item.title: Germany: Gen Z Protests Against Cost of Living Turn Violent in Several Cities
item.description: Protests against the rising cost of living, initially sparked in France, have reached Germany, involving tens of thousands of young people in numerous cities. Some demonstrations escalated into clashes with police, particularly in Cologne and Hamburg, where water cannons and special forces were deployed. Protesters cited concerns over living costs, education funding, environmental issues, and potential military conscription.

item.title: Polish Prime Minister Accuses President Amid Constitutional Tribunal Crisis
item.description: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk addressed the nation, accusing the opposition party 'Law and Justice' and President Andrzej Duda of violence against Constitutional Tribunal members and undermining the rule of law. Tusk refused compromise, stating the tribunal must operate independently and constitutionally.

item.title: US Open to Playing Role in Pakistan-Afghanistan Security Concerns, Says Senator Rubio
item.description: Senator Marco Rubio indicated US willingness to play a constructive role in addressing Pakistan's security concerns regarding alleged attacks from Afghan territory. Washington opposes terrorism regardless of its origin or target.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Allow AI to Manage Financial Transactions Up to a Set Limit
item.description: Kazakhstan is preparing to allow citizens to conduct daily financial operations using artificial intelligence. Digital assistants will be able to pay utility bills, purchase groceries, and book flight tickets. The National Bank stated that AI can handle transactions up to 50-60 thousand tenge, saving citizens time.

item.title: Over 40,000 Chronic Kidney Disease Patients Under Medical Supervision in Kazakhstan
item.description: More than 40,000 patients suffering from chronic kidney disease are currently under medical observation in Kazakhstan. This highlights a significant public health concern within the country.

item.title: Trump Claims Iran Seeks Deal, Negotiations Progressing Well
item.description: Former U.S. President Donald Trump stated that Iran is seeking a deal and that negotiations are proceeding favorably. This comment comes amid ongoing discussions regarding Iran's nuclear program and international relations.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Foreign Trade Deficit Reaches $13.7 Billion in Nine Months
item.description: Uzbekistan's foreign trade deficit reached $13.7 billion in the first nine months of the year. Exports decreased due to a sharp decline in gold sales, while imports significantly increased. The total foreign trade turnover amounted to $65.4 billion during the period.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan may lift electricity consumption limits in 2-2.5 years, says President
item.description: Kyrgyzstan could see electricity consumption limits lifted within two to two and a half years, according to President Sadyr Japarov. He stated this while meeting with residents in the Jalal-Abad region. This forecast addresses concerns about power limitations for the population.
